title: Mobile Gaming May Hurt Your Neck and Elbows
paragraphs: Mobile gaming is a huge market, with over 3 billion people playing games on their phones. In fact, mobile games accounted for a little over half the global gaming market in 2025, making $116 billion.

Too much time gaming on your phone could impact your health though, with those showing signs of mobile gaming addiction — a problem in itself — being more likely to experience pain in their backs, necks, elbows and wrists.
A study in The Open Public Health Journal used survey data from 364 students to understand the links between mobile gaming addiction and musculoskeletal pain.
The participants answered questions about their gaming habits designed to look for signs of addiction. They were also asked about their musculoskeletal health, including any pain they had.

The researchers said 34 students — or 9% of the participants — met the criteria for mobile gaming addiction. Also, half of all participants reported experiencing some kind of musculoskeletal pain in the seven days before doing the survey.
However, gaming addicted students were much more likely to feel pain — and more likely to feel it in certain areas.

Among those who'd felt pain over the last week, 85% of addicted participants reported neck pain, compared with 65% of their non-addicted peers. Among those experiencing pain, 65% of gaming addicted students also reported upper back pain, while 55% of non-addicts did.

Forty-one percent of gaming addicts with pain reported hand or wrist pain, versus 34% of non-addicts. Finally, the biggest difference between the two groups was elbow pain — 41% of gaming addicts with pain had it, compared with 13% of non-addicted students.
A lot of these differences are likely because of the awkward way people hold their phones to game, and the repetitive movements they make while playing.
The researchers called for university health programs to include messaging on taking breaks from gaming, and to provide support for students using games to deal with stress.
